title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own manuscript. It is a typed Bourbaki draft: the header reads '4 - 40 -' and 'n° 392', it is typed, and it uses Bourbaki's internal cross-reference style ('chap. II, § 3, n° 2', 'chap. IV, § 1, n° 2', 'n° 3, th. 3', 'n° 4, lemme 2'). It belongs to the material that became Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative ch. VII (Diviseurs), §4, on modules over Krull domains. It has been filed between pages 48 and 50 of Grothendieck's handwritten notes on the functional equation of L-functions, which deal with duality of the middle extension E_η^♮ and local correction terms μ_x(E). The typed page has no mathematical relation to those neighbours.

Setting.
- A is a Krull domain with fraction field K, and P is the set of its height-one primes.
- For 𝔭 in P, A_𝔭 is a DVR with residue field k(𝔭).
- M is a finitely generated, torsion-free (in fact lattice/reflexive) A-module of rank n, with V = K⊗M and M(𝔭) = M_𝔭/𝔭M_𝔭.

Lemma 7 (end of its statement and its proof). Let x_1,…,x_m in M be K-linearly independent and let L = Σ A x_i, a free and hence reflexive module.
- (a) The images x_i(𝔭) are k(𝔭)-linearly independent for almost all 𝔭.
- (b) They are independent for all 𝔭 in P if and only if M/L is torsion-free.

Proof of (a). Complete the x_i to a K-basis x_1,…,x_n of V and let N be the free module they span. Two lattices agree at almost all 𝔭, so N_𝔭 = M_𝔭 for almost all 𝔭. At such 𝔭 the x_i(𝔭) form a basis of M(𝔭).

Proof of (b), forward direction. If M/L is torsion-free, then M_𝔭/L_𝔭 is torsion-free over the DVR A_𝔭, hence free. So L_𝔭 is a direct summand of M_𝔭, which gives dim L(𝔭) = m and the x_i(𝔭) are independent.

Proof of (b), converse. Independence of the x_i(𝔭) plus Nakayama gives that L_𝔭 is a direct summand of M_𝔭. Hence (M/L)_𝔭 is torsion-free, so Ass(M/L) ∩ P = ∅. Since L is reflexive, Ass(M/L) ⊂ P ∪ {(0)}. Therefore Ass(M/L) = {(0)} and M/L is torsion-free.

Lemma 8. If the rank is at least 2, there exists x ≠ 0 with M/Ax torsion-free.
- Take y ≠ 0. The set Y of 𝔭 with y(𝔭) = 0 is finite by Lemma 7.
- If Y is empty, M/Ay is torsion-free by Lemma 7.
- Otherwise localize at S = ∩_{𝔭∈Y}(A − 𝔭). Then S^{-1}A is a semilocal Krull domain with finitely many height-one primes, hence a PID; the page breaks off here.

Purpose. This feeds the standard structure theorem: a reflexive (or torsion-free) finitely generated module over a Krull domain contains a free submodule L with M/L isomorphic to an ideal. Over a Dedekind domain this gives the Steinitz form M ≅ A^{n-1} ⊕ 𝔞.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. Implicit hypotheses: M_𝔭 is free over the DVR A_𝔭, which holds since M is finitely generated and torsion-free; this is needed for the Nakayama direct-summand argument. L is reflexive because it is free on K-independent generators.
Archival note: this typed Bourbaki page is unrelated to the surrounding handwritten L-function pages 48 and 50, and appears to be misfiled or reused paper.

ideas.what: For a lattice M and K-independent elements x_i, the reductions x_i(𝔭) are independent at almost all height-one primes, and at all of them if and only if M/L is torsion-free.
ideas.modern_name: Lattices over Krull domains; criterion for a free submodule to be saturated (pure)

ideas.what: Existence of x ≠ 0 with M/Ax torsion-free when rank ≥ 2, via semilocalization at finitely many height-one primes, which yields a PID.
ideas.modern_name: Unimodular/saturated element; step toward 'M contains a free L with M/L isomorphic to an ideal'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bourbaki AC VII §4 (generalizing Steinitz for Dedekind domains)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard Bourbaki draft page of Commutative Algebra ch. VII, with routine results that were published there. The only point of interest is archival: a Bourbaki typescript sits inside Grothendieck's L-function notes.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is accurate. The header '4 - 40 -' and 'n° 392' denote the Bourbaki draft numbering, not Grothendieck's pagination; the handwritten '49' in the bottom-left corner is the archive page number.
Underlining in the original marks the statements of Lemma 7 and Lemma 8 and the word 'Exemple'; this is cosmetic only.
